Objective:¶

In FY 2016, the OFLC processed 775,979 employer applications for 1,699,957 positions for temporary and permanent labor certifications. This was a nine percent increase in the overall number of processed applications from the previous year. The process of reviewing every case is becoming a tedious task as the number of applicants is increasing every year.

The increasing number of applicants every year calls for a Machine Learning based solution that can help in shortlisting the candidates having a higher chance of VISA approval. OFLC has hired the firm EasyVisa for data-driven solutions. You, as a data scientist at EasyVisa, have to analyze the data provided and, with the help of a classification model:

  • Facilitate the process of visa approvals.
  • Recommend a suitable profile for the applicants for whom the visa should be certified or denied based on the drivers that significantly influence the case status.

Key Observations¶

  1. Target Variable Class Imbalance: About 67% of cases are certified and 33% are denied. While unbalanced, it is within a manageable range for machine learning.
  2. The Education Factor: High-school graduates show the lowest visa approval rates, whereas doctorate and master's degree holders show an overwhelming certification rate.
  3. Experience Benefits: Applicants with prior job experience (has_job_experience_Y) have significantly better certification outcomes than those without it.
  4. Prevailing Wages: Certified visas show slightly higher median prevailing wages compared to denied cases.

numerical_cols = ['no_of_employees', 'prevailing_wage']

for col in numerical_cols:
    Q1 = data[col].quantile(0.25)
    Q3 = data[col].quantile(0.75)
    IQR = Q3 - Q1

    lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
    upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR

    outliers = data[(data[col] < lower_bound) |
                    (data[col] > upper_bound)]

    print(f"\n{col}")
    print("Lower Bound:", lower_bound)
    print("Upper Bound:", upper_bound)
    print("Number of Outliers:", len(outliers))

Model building - Original Data¶

In [109]:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

X = data.drop('case_status', axis = 1)
y = data['case_status']

X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size = 0.20, random_state = 1, stratify = y)
print("Training Data Shape:", X_train.shape)
print("Testing Data Shape:", X_test.shape)

Training Data Shape: (20384, 19)
Testing Data Shape: (5096, 19)
In [110]:
models = {'Decision Tree': DecisionTreeClassifier(random_state=1), 'Random Forest': RandomForestClassifier(random_state=1, n_jobs=-1),
          'Bagging Classifier': BaggingClassifier(random_state=1, n_jobs=-1), 'AdaBoost': AdaBoostClassifier(random_state=1), 'Gradient Boosting': GradientBoostingClassifier(random_state=1)}
In [111]:
original_results = []

for name, model in models.items():
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
    y_prob = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1]

    original_results.append({
        'Model': name,
        'Accuracy': accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred),
        'Precision': precision_score(y_test, y_pred),
        'Recall': recall_score(y_test, y_pred),
        'F1 Score': f1_score(y_test, y_pred),
        'ROC-AUC': roc_auc_score(y_test, y_prob)})

original_results_df = pd.DataFrame(original_results)
original_results_df.round(3)

Model Performance Improvement Using Hyperparameter Tuning¶

  1. Decision Tree - Tuning tree depth, minimum samples per split and leaf size can control overfitting and improve generalization.
  2. Random Forest - Optimizing the number of trees, tree depth and feature selection can improve ensemble performance and prediction stability.
  3. Gradient Boosting - Tuning learning rate, number of estimators and tree depth can improve the model's ability to capture complex patterns.
In [ ]:
from sklearn.model_selection import RandomizedSearchCV, StratifiedKFold
from imblearn.pipeline import Pipeline
In [ ]:
sampling_method = 'smote'

if sampling_method == 'smote':
    sampler = SMOTE(random_state=1)

elif sampling_method == 'undersampling':
    sampler = RandomUnderSampler(random_state=1)

elif sampling_method == 'original':
    sampler = 'passthrough'

else:
    raise ValueError("Invalid sampling method")

Model Selection¶

Based on our comparative evaluation of the models before and after hyperparameter tuning (using SMOTE-oversampled training data), the Random Forest Classifier (After Tuning) and the Gradient Boosting Classifier (After Tuning) emerged as our top performers, achieving the highest F1 Macro (~0.697) and ROC-AUC (~0.768) scores.

  • Final Chosen Model: Random Forest Classifier (After Tuning)
  • Performance Summary on the Test Set:
    • Accuracy: ~73.7% — The model correctly predicts visa status for roughly 74 out of 100 applications.
    • Precision: ~79.1% — Out of all cases labeled as 'Certified' by our model, 79% are indeed Certified. This ensures low false-positive instances, meaning the OFLC won't accidentally fast-track high-risk cases that should be denied.
    • Recall: ~82.3% — Out of all actual visas that should have been certified, our model successfully catches 82.3%. This is a strong indicator of efficiency for facilitating and speeding up the approvals of genuine profiles.
    • F1-Score: ~0.807 — Demonstrates a balanced compromise between precision and recall.
    • ROC-AUC: ~0.768 — Shows reliable discriminative capacity between certified and denied applications.

Actionable Insights & Recommendations¶

  • Automated Screening Tier: Establish an automatic fast-track queue for applicants possessing Master's / Doctorate degrees combined with prior job experience and a market-rate prevailing wage. This reduces manual labor for highly qualified individuals.
  • Flag High-Risk Cases: Applications with High School education, no job experience, and/or sub-standard wages should be automatically routed to senior case officers for rigorous audit, as these are statistically less likely to meet certifications criteria.
  • Wage Compliance checks: Programmatically validate the prevailing_wage against geographic and industry standard indexes during entry submission to reject or flag low-wage applications immediately.
  • Training Program Requirements: Since the lack of job experience negatively affects status, the OFLC can advise employers to actively sponsor or integrate 'Job Training Programs' (requires_job_training_Y) for entry-level foreign workers to offset the negative impact of missing prior experience.
